text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Saturday and Monday:

- Switzerland's Free Democrats issued a statement saying they want 101 million Swiss francs from the government's investment plan to be used towards making schools and education programs more efficient.

- Roger de Weck, editor-in-chief of Zurich's daily Tages-Anzeiger, announced his resignation at the weekend, saying it is because he opposes the paper's planned budget cuts. - Representatives of the Sinti and Roma gypsies in Switzerland sent a letter to Swiss President Arnold Koller saying they are disappointed that the groups are not included in the Holocaust-funds.
- Philippe Bruggiser, CEO of the SAirGroup, said further tough savings measures may have to be reckoned with in order to keep the airline afloat.
- Over 55,000 people in Switzerland had been officially unemployed for over one year by the end of March in Switzerland. - Steel group Moos reported a loss of 187.4 million Swiss francs for 1996.
- Swiss National Bank President Hans Meyer said he does not expect a quick pickup in Switzerland's economy.
- The number of practicing medical doctors in Switzerland rose by 1.6 percent in 1996.
